name: New Lenox
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in New Lenox, IL 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in New Lenox, IL: free Christmas in the Commons with Santa, lights and skating, park district Winter Wonderland and Breakfast with Santa.
lede: New Lenox does Christmas at its Village Commons, where a giant lighted Santa and a lighted penguin named Floyd greet families. On December weekends the village adds free visits with Santa, skating and wagon rides beside Village Hall.
celebrates: New Lenox celebrates around the Village Commons at 101 Veterans Parkway. The village fills the Commons with a holiday light display, and on Saturdays and Sundays in December it runs Christmas in the Commons, a free festival with visits with Santa in the Village Hall rotunda, horse-drawn wagon rides, synthetic ice skating, a holiday market, holiday characters and food trucks. On other days families can drive through to see the lights. The New Lenox Community Park District adds Winter Wonderland with Santa, pizza and a North Pole mailbox, St. Jude parish serves Breakfast with Santa, and the public library plans holiday programs such as a Grinch movie afternoon and a family gingerbread house craft.
lastyear: In November 2025 the village revealed the newest piece of its display, a lighted penguin named Floyd. Patch reported that crews began building him on a Thursday before Thanksgiving, and Mayor Tim Baldermann said the village budgets to add to the display every year, with Floyd costing $115,000. The village said Floyd stands 36 feet tall with 38,186 LED lights. Christmas in the Commons was planned for Saturdays and Sundays starting December 6, 2025, from 4 to 8 pm, with free admission.
facts: New Lenox Township was created in 1852, when the Rock Island Railroad was built between Chicago and Rock Island. The village was platted in 1858 under the name Tracy, after the railroad's general superintendent, but Tracy asked for another name. In 1863 the town took the name New Lenox from the township, which supervisor J. Van Duser had named after his hometown of Lenox, New York. In 1898 the first rural Bell telephone company in Illinois opened in New Lenox, and the village was incorporated in 1946.
trains: New Lenox grew up beside the tracks. The Rock Island Railroad arrived in 1852, and the historical society notes that a depot built around 1903 replaced the original frame depot and now serves Metra. Today the village has two Metra stops: the Route 30 station on the Rock Island line and the Laraway Road station on the SouthWest Service. From 1907 a trolley also ran between Joliet and Chicago Heights. Each December the CASA Christmas Express leaves the New Lenox Metra station for a Santa visit in Tinley Park.

kidfact: New Lenox was almost called Tracy. The railroad boss it was named for asked the town to pick a different name, so it borrowed New Lenox from the township.
faq: Where is Christmas in the Commons in New Lenox?

It takes place at the New Lenox Village Commons, 101 Veterans Parkway, beside Village Hall just off Route 30. The village fills the Commons with a holiday light display and runs the festival on Saturday and Sunday evenings in December. Santa visits happen inside Village Hall, in the rotunda on the first floor.
Is Christmas in the Commons free?

Yes. The village says the event does not require a ticket, and visits with Santa are free with no registration. There is no photographer, so families bring their own phone or camera. Food trucks, vendors and the holiday market sell items, and many take cards and mobile payment, but the village suggests bringing cash as a backup.
Can we drive through the New Lenox Christmas lights?

Yes, on any day the event is not running. The road through the Commons closes to traffic on the Saturdays and Sundays when Christmas in the Commons is held, so on those evenings, from 4 to 8 pm, families stroll through the display on foot. On the other days of the season the lights can be seen from the car.
Is the skating rink at the Commons real ice?

No. The village says the rink is synthetic ice, so it is open in any temperature, and standard ice skates work on it. Ice skating is one of the activities the village lists for Christmas in the Commons, which runs on Saturday and Sunday evenings in December from 4 to 8 pm.
Is there a quiet way to see Santa in New Lenox?

Yes. The village offers Quiet Santa visits for children with a disability or other needs that make lines or crowds hard. Families email the village at least 72 hours before their planned visit to set up a calmer time. Regular visits with Santa take place in the Village Hall rotunda during Christmas in the Commons.
